cohort_answer.text:
Acyclovir over valacyclovir: HSV meningitis/encephalitis.
Valganciclovir over valacyclovir: Herpes B treatment better activity, CMV treatment.
Famciclovir over acyclovir: Uncomplicated zoster (famciclovir higher oral bioavailability than acyclovir, dosed TID rather than 5 times daily).

Azithromycin over clarithromycin: Better for gram-negatives, esp. M catarrhalis and H flu.
Ampicillin over cloxacillin: Enterococci, Listeria.
Cefazolin over cloxacillin: Surgical prophylaxis, penicillin allergy, AIN, heart failure.

questions.model_answer:
a) Better renal penetration: Cefazolin over cloxacillin (cefazolin achieves high urinary concentrations; cloxacillin is highly protein-bound with poor urinary penetration).
b) Cover bacterial meningitis: Ampicillin over cloxacillin (ampicillin covers Listeria monocytogenes and achieves adequate CSF penetration; cloxacillin does not cover Listeria and penetrates the CNS poorly).
c) Patient has G6PD deficiency: Atovaquone over dapsone (dapsone causes oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency).
d) Patient on carbamazepine: Fluconazole over caspofungin (carbamazepine is an enzyme inducer that reduces caspofungin exposure, requiring dose adjustment; fluconazole avoids this interaction).
e) Not a drug that treats C. difficile and not strongly associated with causing C. difficile: Doxycycline over TMP-SMX (doxycycline carries one of the lowest C. difficile risks among commonly used antibiotics and does not treat CDI).
f) Better activity for CMV: Valganciclovir over valacyclovir (valganciclovir is a ganciclovir prodrug with potent CMV activity; valacyclovir has only modest/prophylactic CMV activity and is primarily an HSV/VZV agent).

questions.question: PM 10. Mechanism of antivirals. Where do the following act (3): Foscarnet, Cidofovir, Maribavir, Letermovir

parts.text: State the mechanism/target of each antiviral

cohort_answer.text: Foscarnet - DNA polymerase inhibitor; UL54, binds pyrophosphate binding site, inhibits transcription. Cidofovir - intracellularly activated to diphosphate form; competitive DNA polymerase inhibition and incorporated into viral DNA causing chain termination. Maribavir - UL97 phosphokinase inhibitor, inhibits viral DNA synthesis and blocks nuclear egress of virions. Letermovir - UL56, inhibits DNA terminase enzyme complex, stops splicing and virion assembly.

questions.question: Antiviral drugs against Herpesviruses / CMV.

parts.text: Mechanism of action of Ganciclovir
2 mechanisms of resistance to Ganciclovir
Mechanism of action of Foscarnet (pyrophosphate analogs)
Mechanism of action of Acyclovir
Mechanism of action of Letermovir (CMV terminase complex inhibitor)

cohort_answer.text: Ganciclovir: competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate to inhibit viral DNA polymerase and block viral DNA synthesis; primarily reserved for CMV, also active against HSV-1/2 (same mechanism as valganciclovir). Resistance: UL97 gene mutation (most common, occurs prior to UL54, causes deficiency in viral kinase for ganciclovir phosphorylation/activation, cidofovir and foscarnet usually retain efficacy) and UL54 mutation (often co-exists with UL97, changes viral DNA polymerase, cross-resistance to cidofovir common, cross-resistance to foscarnet rare; HSV isolates resistant to acyclovir due to absent TK are also resistant to ganciclovir). Foscarnet: inorganic pyrophosphate analog, selectively inhibits viral DNA polymerase by blocking pyrophosphate binding sites, suppressing viral replication; resistance occurs secondary to some but not all UL54 mutations; primarily reserved for ganciclovir-resistant CMV, also effective against HSV/VZV including acyclovir-resistant isolates; main adverse effect is nephrotoxicity (dose-limiting, minimized with hydration). Acyclovir: synthetic purine nucleoside analog with high affinity for HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV thymidine kinase which phosphorylates/activates the drug; human cellular guanylate kinase further phosphorylates it to acyclovir triphosphate, which blocks viral DNA synthesis by competitively inhibiting/inactivating viral DNA polymerase and causing DNA chain termination (valacyclovir, penciclovir, famciclovir have similar mechanisms; cidofovir similar but does not require viral TK). Letermovir: inhibits the CMV terminase complex (novel mechanism), which normally cleaves long DNA chains produced during CMV replication into single functional units; only active against CMV; FDA approved for CMV prophylaxis in adult CMV-seropositive allogeneic HSCT recipients; low barrier to resistance in vitro; no dosage adjustment needed with CrCl >10 mL/min.

parts.text: CMV. What is the mechanism of action of ganciclovir, foscarnet, and letermovir? What are two gene mutations for ganciclovir and the location in the cell impacted?

questions.model_answer: Mechanisms of action: Ganciclovir - a guanosine nucleoside analogue that is first phosphorylated by the CMV-encoded UL97 protein kinase (and then by cellular kinases) to its active triphosphate form, which competitively inhibits the viral DNA polymerase (UL54) and causes chain termination. Foscarnet - a pyrophosphate analogue that directly (without requiring intracellular phosphorylation) binds the pyrophosphate-binding site of the viral DNA polymerase, blocking cleavage of pyrophosphate from nucleoside triphosphates and inhibiting DNA chain elongation. Letermovir - inhibits the CMV terminase complex (pUL56/pUL89/pUL51), blocking viral DNA cleavage and packaging into capsids (does not inhibit the DNA polymerase). Two gene mutations for ganciclovir resistance and their cellular impact: (1) UL97 mutation - affects the viral kinase responsible for the initial phosphorylation step of ganciclovir (cytoplasmic activation step, most common cause of resistance, low-to-moderate level); (2) UL54 mutation - affects the viral DNA polymerase itself (the ultimate drug target), causing higher-level resistance and potential cross-resistance to cidofovir and/or foscarnet depending on mutation location.

parts.text: Given a Table. Fill in 2 most common mutations for CMV resistance, whether or not you would use the below therapy in the setting of the named mutation. Columns: Mutation, High dose Gancyclovir, Foscarnet, Cidofovir. Rows: 1. 2.

questions.model_answer: Two most common CMV resistance mutations: (1) UL97 mutation - confers resistance to ganciclovir (reduced viral kinase-mediated phosphorylation); high-dose ganciclovir may still be tried for low-grade mutations but is often inadequate; foscarnet - still active (does not require UL97 phosphorylation), can use; cidofovir - still active (activated by cellular, not viral, kinases), can use. (2) UL54 (DNA polymerase) mutation - confers resistance to ganciclovir; high-dose ganciclovir - generally not effective; foscarnet - variable, some UL54 mutations retain foscarnet susceptibility, others confer cross-resistance (use with caution/confirm susceptibility); cidofovir - often cross-resistant (shares the polymerase target), generally avoid unless susceptibility confirmed.

parts.text: Asked for target for site of action if ganciclovir, foscarnet and Maribavir

questions.model_answer: Site of action: Ganciclovir - viral DNA polymerase (UL54), after activation via phosphorylation by the UL97 kinase. Foscarnet - viral DNA polymerase (UL54), acting directly at the pyrophosphate-binding site without requiring phosphorylation. Maribavir - the viral UL97 protein kinase itself, which it inhibits directly, blocking downstream viral DNA synthesis, capsid nuclear egress, and CMV gene expression.

questions.question: CMV drugs.

parts.text: What is the MOA of valganciclovir, foscarnet, and letermovir?
Give two mutations for CMV for ganciclovir resistance and their viral targets.

questions.model_answer: a) MOA: Valganciclovir (prodrug of ganciclovir) - phosphorylated by viral UL97 kinase then host kinases to triphosphate form, competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase (UL54) and causes chain termination. Foscarnet - pyrophosphate analogue that directly inhibits viral DNA polymerase without requiring phosphorylation. Letermovir - inhibits the HCMV terminase complex (UL51/UL56/UL89), blocking viral DNA cleavage/packaging (not a polymerase inhibitor). b) Ganciclovir resistance mutations (2) and viral targets: (1) UL97 mutation - reduces phosphorylation/activation of ganciclovir (kinase target). (2) UL54 mutation - alters viral DNA polymerase itself, reduces ganciclovir binding (and can confer cross-resistance to cidofovir/foscarnet depending on mutation).

questions.question: Foscarnet

parts.text: What is the mechanism of action of foscarnet against i. Herpesviridae and ii. HIV
What are 4 viruses other than HIV for which foscarnet is used for treatment or prophylaxis
What are 4 metabolic derangements associated with foscarnet?

questions.model_answer:
a) Mechanism of action: (i) Herpesviridae - foscarnet is a pyrophosphate analogue that directly binds the pyrophosphate-binding site of the viral DNA polymerase, blocking pyrophosphate cleavage from incoming nucleoside triphosphates and thereby inhibiting DNA chain elongation, without requiring intracellular phosphorylation/activation. (ii) HIV - foscarnet similarly binds the pyrophosphate-binding site of HIV reverse transcriptase, non-competitively inhibiting its function by the same pyrophosphate-analogue mechanism.
b) 4 viruses other than HIV treated/prophylaxed with foscarnet: (1) CMV (particularly ganciclovir-resistant disease), (2) HSV (acyclovir-resistant strains), (3) VZV (acyclovir-resistant strains), (4) HHV-6 (or EBV in select settings).
c) 4 metabolic derangements: (1) hypocalcemia (ionized calcium chelation), (2) hypomagnesemia, (3) hypokalemia, (4) hypophosphatemia (or hyperphosphatemia, both reported).

questions.question: HSV Infection:

parts.text: A) Mutations to what two proteins can cause Acyclovir Resistance?
B) For a swab from a vesicle, what are two tests other than PCR that can make a diagnosis of HSV?

questions.model_answer: a) Two proteins with mutations causing acyclovir resistance: (1) Viral thymidine kinase (TK) - most common mechanism, reduced/absent phosphorylation of acyclovir to active form. (2) Viral DNA polymerase - less common, alters acyclovir triphosphate binding site. b) Two tests other than PCR for HSV diagnosis from a vesicle swab: (1) Viral culture (cell culture with cytopathic effect, historically gold standard though less sensitive than PCR). (2) Direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) staining or Tzanck smear (multinucleated giant cells - less specific/sensitive but rapid).

questions.question: Q74 2023 Day 1. Foscarnet.

parts.text: MOA for treating i) Herpesviridae
MOA for treating ii) HIV
4 other viruses it can be used to treat or prophylax against
4 side effects

cohort_answer.text:
MOA Herpesviridae: Inhibits viral DNA polymerase by binding to the pyrophosphate binding site (non-competitive inhibition).
MOA HIV: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase (acts as an NNRTI).
4 other viruses: CMV - retinitis/encephalitis; HSV resistant to acyclovir; VZV - progressive outer retinal necrosis; Human Herpesvirus 6. (Has activity against all Herpesviridae viruses: HSV, VZV, EBV, CMV, HHV-6, HHV-7, Kaposi; not used for HIV in practice; mainly used for CMV, HSV, VZV resistant disease with TK/UL97 resistance.)
4 side effects: Nephrotoxicity (avoid with other nephrotoxic drugs; azotemia, proteinuria, acute tubular necrosis; give with saline prehydration 1-2L NS 1-2h before dosing); electrolyte abnormalities (chelator of divalent cations - hypocalcemia 15-35%, hypomagnesemia 15-44%, hypokalemia 10-16%; also hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, hyperphosphatemia; monitor electrolytes closely); CNS (seizures 10%, headaches 25%); GI (nausea 47%, diarrhea 30%, vomiting 26%); hematological (anemia 33%, granulocytopenia 17%); fever (65%).

questions.question: Q23 (2008, 2007). HIV patient with recurrent mucocutaneous HSV

parts.text: a) Mechanism of action of acyclovir
b) 2 mechanisms of resistance
c) 2 alternatives and their toxicities

cohort_answer.text: a) Binds DNA polymerase to stop DNA synthesis: acyclovir phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase, then cellular kinase to acyclovir-triphosphate, which competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase as dGTP analog; incorporation causes chain termination. b) Mutation in DNA polymerase (target); mutation in viral kinase (prevents activation, ~90% of resistance); absence of viral TK. c) Foscarnet - nephrotoxic (AKI, ATN, dose related), divalent cation chelation (hypoCa 15-30%, hypoMg 15-45%, hypoK 10-15%, rare hyperCa/hypo-hyperPO). Cidofovir - nephrotoxic (dose related, accumulates in proximal renal tubular cells, Fanconi syndrome), neutropenia 25%.

questions.question: Q28 (2017 PM). Asked for target site of action for ganciclovir, foscarnet, and maribavir

parts.text: State target site of action for each CMV drug

cohort_answer.text: Ganciclovir - inhibits viral DNA polymerase UL54 (via dNTP binding site/catalytic site). Foscarnet - inhibits viral DNA polymerase UL54 (via pyrophosphate binding site). Maribavir - inhibits viral UL97 kinase, preventing nuclear egress. UL97 mutations confer resistance to ganciclovir/valganciclovir; UL54 mutation confers multidrug resistance.

questions.question: Q29 (2018). Letermovir is a new agent used to treat CMV

parts.text: a) What is its target?
b) What is the MOA?

cohort_answer.text: Target: UL56 (component of CMV terminase enzyme complex). Mechanism of Letermovir

2 resistance mutations for CMV to antivirals and target site affected

cohort_answer.text: Ganciclovir - binds UL54 catalytic site of DNA polymerase. Letermovir - binds UL89/56/51 DNA terminase complex, inhibits viral maturation. parts.text: Match the drug-pair choices to the appropriate clinical scenario phrases

questions.model_answer: No specific clinical-scenario phrases were provided in this batch to match against the drug-pair list, so a specific matched answer cannot be given reliably. General rationale for each pair, for reference: Valganciclovir over valacyclovir/acyclovir - superior CMV activity. Famciclovir over acyclovir - once/twice-daily dosing, better bioavailability, similar HSV/VZV coverage. Atovaquone over dapsone - avoids hemolysis in G6PD deficiency. Doxycycline over TMP-SMX - avoided in sulfa allergy, low C. difficile risk. Fluconazole over caspofungin - oral bioavailability/step-down therapy for susceptible Candida, but avoided with strong CYP3A4 interactions (e.g., carbamazepine). Liposomal amphotericin B over amphotericin deoxycholate - reduced nephrotoxicity/infusion reactions. Piperacillin-tazobactam over meropenem - carbapenem-sparing for susceptible organisms. Moxifloxacin over levofloxacin - better CNS penetration and anaerobic coverage. Metronidazole over clindamycin - lower C. difficile risk. Azithromycin over clarithromycin - fewer CYP3A4 drug interactions (e.g., in a patient on carbamazepine or other CYP3A4 substrates). Ampicillin over cloxacillin - preferred for Enterococcus. Cefazolin over cloxacillin - better tolerability/renal penetration for MSSA bacteremia.
